coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app contains substantial risky transformation logic (aggregation, filtering, pagination, sorting, URL serialization) and zero tests of any kind.

signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value tests, per the rubric; but it also means nothing earns its keep.

findings.issue: speciesIndex() builds the home-page index (per-ID type slots, generation mapping, dex ordering) with no tests; a refactor here silently corrupts filtering, counts and pagination on every list page.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest unit tests over this module with a small JSON fixture, asserting filter/count/order outcomes rather than internals.

findings.issue: Filter matching, PAGE_SIZE slicing, page clamping and the homeHref default-omission serialization are untested; off-by-one and query-param regressions would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Export homeHref and the filter logic and test cases like ?type=fire&generation=generation-i, page out of range, and page=1 omission.

findings.issue: sortRows' missing-values-last-in-both-directions rule and aria-sort state are untested; a rewrite of the comparator (e.g. dropping the sign-independent null branch) passes unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Export sortRows (it is already a pure function) and cover each column, both directions, and null values.

findings.issue: moveTables() (version-group filtering, method ranking with alphabetical fallback, default game = highest order, ?game override) is untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract into the lib layer and unit-test against a trimmed pokemon.moves fixture.

findings.issue: cardsFor's alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000), ID-based dedup and dex sort are unguarded; type/move/ability card lists could regress to include Mega forms or duplicates.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test cardsFor with mixed refs including IDs above 10000 and duplicate entries.

findings.issue: The debounced search-to-URL sync and the useTask$ back/forward re-sync (activeElement guard) are untested client-side URL-state logic.
findings.suggestion: Add a component-level test (Playwright component testing or Vitest browser mode) covering type-then-wait navigation, Enter-submit, and back/forward restore.

findings.issue: The request cache (60s TTL, 404-as-null caching, error eviction via value.catch) has no tests; a change could cache failures or serve stale data after API_BASE_URL changes.
findings.suggestion: Test api() with a stubbed fetch for 404, 500, and cache-hit behaviour.

findings.issue: latestFlavorText's whitespace collapsing and last-English-entry rule, and orDash's missing-value rendering (app/src/lib/format.ts:24), are untested; the em-dash rule is easy to break in a cleanup pass.
findings.suggestion: These are trivially unit-testable pure functions; add table-driven tests.

findings.issue: Not-found paths (status(404) from loaders and the catch-all route) are untested in-app; a route refactor could render NotFound with a 200 status or drop it entirely.
findings.suggestion: Add one SSR-level test that /pokemon/missingno renders the Not found heading and returns 404.

findings.issue: All key helpers (humanize, dexNumber, pageTitle, orDash) are module-private to their files' consumers and untested; format.ts is testable but the riskier ones (homeHref, sortRows, moveTables) are not exported at all, raising the cost of adding tests later.
findings.suggestion: Export the pure logic from routes/components into lib and pair each with unit tests; also add a vitest script to app/package.json.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own: no test script, no runner dependency, no spec files. Almost all its risk lives in untested pure logic — index aggregation, filtering/pagination, moves-table sorting, URL serialization — and none of it is exported for later testing. Any refactor of the data layer would pass today's in-app checks, which is nothing.
